front.title: Receiver-Driven Credit Control (RDCC) for Many-to-One Traffic in Distributed Inference Networks

abstract.t: Expert-parallel and disaggregated (prefill/decode) inference deployments generate many-to-one ("incast") traffic in which many senders transmit to one receiver at the same time. Mitigations based on priority queues, enlarged switch buffers, and disabled Explicit Congestion Notification (ECN) marking stop scaling when the bandwidth-delay product of the network grows. This document specifies Receiver-Driven Credit Control (RDCC), a UDP-based signaling protocol with which a receiver bounds the volume of data that all senders may have in flight toward it. RDCC defines a receiver credit budget, a bounded unscheduled first window for short messages, cumulative per-message and class-weighted credit grants, sender backlog indications with suggested credit rates, and optional congestion reports from on-path nodes. RDCC operates within a limited domain, complements the congestion control of the data transport, and does not change the format of data packets.
